# Convex vs Non-Convex Loss Landscapes

Understanding convex vs. non-convex loss landscapes explains when gradient descent has theoretical guarantees, why saddle points matter, why deep networks avoid bad local minima, and what flatness means for generalisation.

## Convex Functions

f(λx + (1−λ)y) ≤ λf(x) + (1−λ)f(y). Key property: any local minimum is a global minimum. Gradient inequality: f(y) ≥ f(x) + ∇f(x)ᵀ(y−x). Examples: linear regression, logistic regression, SVM.

Strong convexity: f(y) ≥ f(x) + ∇f(x)ᵀ(y−x) + (μ/2)‖y−x‖² → unique global minimum, linear convergence.

## Jensen's Inequality

E[f(X)] ≥ f(E[X]). Foundation of ELBO: log p(x) ≥ E_q[log p(x,z)/q(z)] = ELBO (Jensen applied to log-concave p).

## Saddle Points

∇f=0, indefinite Hessian (mixed eigenvalue signs). Gradient descent stalls near saddle points. Escape time ∝ 1/|λ_min|. Proportion of local minima vs saddle points decreases exponentially with dimension.

| Critical Point | Hessian | Behaviour |
|----------------|---------|-----------|
| Local min | PD | Convergence |
| Local max | ND | Unstable, escape |
| Saddle | Indefinite | Slow escape |

## No Bad Local Minima in Deep Networks

In high dimensions, probability all n Hessian eigenvalues positive decays exponentially in n. Nearly all critical points are saddle points. Overparameterised networks have a connected manifold of zero-loss global minima.

## Flat vs. Sharp Minima

Large Hessian eigenvalues → sharp minima → poor generalisation under weight perturbation. Flat minima (small λ_max) → stable under perturbation → better test performance.

## Mode Connectivity

Different random initialisation optima are connected by loss-preserving paths in weight space. Loss landscape is not isolated minima — it is a connected flat manifold.

## Neural Tangent Kernel

Width → ∞: network linearises, loss landscape becomes convex quadratic. NTK K(x,x') = ∇_θf(x)ᵀ∇_θf(x') stays constant. Explains why overparameterised networks converge easily.
